% Shared normative assumptions, input contract, and dependency rules.
\section{Inputs, assumptions, and dependency gates}\label{sec:inputs}

\subsection{Stage-specific lifecycle and record model}\label{sec:input-record}

The producer lifecycle is one ordered vocabulary, not a claim that every
request visits every state:
\path{not_requested}, \path{requested}, \path{effective},
\path{unavailable}, \path{resolved}, \path{applied},
\path{fit_realized}, \path{complete_publication_candidate},
\path{publication_decided}, \path{published}, \path{failed},
\path{not_produced}, and \path{superseded}. Here \path{requested} is the
immutable request and requested parent/method/use identities;
\path{effective} means every sentinel and requested option has one explicit
effective value or typed unavailable state; \path{resolved} means one exact
compatible method, route, support, objective, weighting, constraints,
fallback, and failure plan is selected and frozen; \path{applied} means that
resolved procedure was invoked for one exact attempt; and
\path{fit_realized} means immutable numerical fit values, role states,
residual, and execution outcome were produced.

\path{complete_publication_candidate} means every required value-or-status
role, identity, cause, and provenance member is structurally complete for
POINT publication evaluation. \path{publication_decided} means the
POINT-owned fit-publication/completeness decision artifact exists, and
\path{published} means the accepted immutable candidate is exposed under its
exact product role. If an execution-attempt identity named
\path{fit_attempted} is retained in a representation, it is evidence beneath
\path{applied}, never a competing producer-lifecycle state.

Eight logical records shall remain separate even if one representation stores
them together:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\Alph*.]
\item \textbf{Request and parent record}: immutable observation, array,
requested parent/method/use identities, exact parent science and provenance,
source reference, requested search/fit domains, requested options, constraints,
support/weight requests, and unresolved sentinels.
\item \textbf{Effective-configuration record}: every resolved sentinel and
effective search, fit-domain, support, weight, constraint, and option value or
typed unavailable state.
\item \textbf{Resolved-method/plan record}: one frozen method, route, support,
objective, weighting, constraints, fallback, comparison, termination, and
failure plan.
\item \textbf{Application-attempt record}: applied plan identity, attempt
identity, invocation time/state, branch/restart/retry identity, and execution
outcome.
\item \textbf{Realized-fit and component record}: selected seed, fitted
values, component states, association outcome, realized constraints, residual,
diagnostics, response/bias/uncertainty states, causes, and provenance.
\item \textbf{Publication-candidate record}: every required value-or-status
POINT role with identity, cause, provenance, and structural-completeness state;
the POINT publication state; and the identities and statuses of linked
requested decisions where required, without requiring successful realization
of every downstream named use.
\item \textbf{Publication decision}: POINT-owned fit-completeness profile,
decision, reasons, decision identity, lifecycle, and provenance.
\item \textbf{Published product record}: exact accepted immutable candidate,
product role, version, generation, inherited parent observation/exposure
lineage or typed \path{not_applicable}, lifecycle, and provenance. POINT creates
no exposure identity. Per-array results from one observation preserve common
exposure and reference terms; any aggregate requires separate dependence
authority.
\end{enumerate}

The request and parent record shall not require a selected seed, fitted
centroid or parameters, association outcome, realized constraint or residual,
or applied/fit-realized outcome. Those facts belong only to later records.
An early stop preserves only the records and lifecycle states actually
reached. Its exact terminal outcome is \path{unavailable}, \path{failed}, or
\path{not_produced} with cause as applicable; it shall not fabricate
\path{applied}, \path{fit_realized}, or any later state, and it shall not
silently delete a requested row.

Every route boundary instance shall additionally bind its exact predecessor
package/version/source digest, signal role, owner approval,
compatibility/supersession status, source morphology, exact parent-response
identity and status (including typed unavailability),
processed-map profile, Gaussian compatibility, response-center relation,
model-mismatch state, expected centroid bias or typed unavailability,
fit-domain relation, and displacement-claim status.

\subsection{Method authorities and present availability}\label{sec:method-authorities}

The base operator identity is \MethodID. Its numerical realization is gated
by three scientifically and lifecycle-distinct records:

\begin{longtable}{@{}p{0.29\linewidth}p{0.18\linewidth}p{0.45\linewidth}@{}}
\toprule
Authority & Current state & Consequence \\
\midrule
\endhead
\CompatMethod & pending separate owner approval & No numerical fit or fit-derived product. The future record must bind model parameterization, rows, objective, weights, support, search, initialization, association, fallback, constraints, solver-independent resolution, termination, rank, identifiability, sentinel, failure, identity, and compatibility status. \\
\FormalMethod & pending separate owner approval & Marginal formal errors, formal standardization, and formal-uncertainty-dependent uses are unavailable. An otherwise authorized fit is not erased. Joint covariance remains unavailable unless separately authorized. \\
\RMSMethod & pending separate owner approval & Only \path{fitted_amplitude_over_full_map_rms} and exact legacy alias \path{sig2noise} are blocked. An otherwise authorized fit, displacement, effective shape, or formal error is not erased. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

The exact numerical parent-route instances, registered named-use profiles,
fixed-branch response, POINT-full-procedure/parent-fixed response, whole-chain
full-procedure response, and observational bias/accuracy
are also unavailable. No familiar practice, optimizer output, method name,
finite value, or adjacent-package analogy may fill any gap.

\subsection{Exact fit-weight object}\label{sec:fit-weights}

$W_{\mathrm{fit}}$ is the exact object consumed by the compatibility fit. Its
approved source may be uniform, reliability-derived, covariance-derived,
inverse covariance, or another explicitly authorized construction. The source
role and the consumed object are not aliases, although an authority may define
an explicit derivation from one to the other. Every such derivation binds an
identity, source and target units, normalization, support, lifecycle state,
claim ceiling, and provenance. Reliability, covariance, inverse covariance,
and the formal-error model remain scientifically distinct; none is inferred
from another by naming or storage reuse.

\subsection{Product and claim dependency matrix}\label{sec:dependencies}

\small
\begin{longtable}{@{}p{0.25\linewidth}p{0.43\linewidth}p{0.24\linewidth}@{}}
\toprule
Product or claim & Required available facts & Blocking result \\
\midrule
\endhead
Fit result & Exact numerical parent and tangent metric; approved compatibility method; admitted support; objective and exact $W_{\mathrm{fit}}$ mapping; exact parent-response identity/status; successful realization; component states & No numerical fit or fit-derived product. A numerical response is required only when the method or claim requires it; typed response unavailability can coexist with the fit. \\
Fit components & Conforming fit and exact component-identifiability state & Only the affected component is unavailable or failed; conforming siblings remain. \\
Source association & Exact source-reference authority and branch-independent method/domain & Source attribution is unavailable or failed. \\
Processed-map displacement & Fitted centroid; expected position; identical tangent chart/basis; established association & No source-attributed displacement. Response and centroid bias may be typed unavailable but remain visible. \\
Fit-amplitude component & Conforming fitted $A$ role, exact parent unit/calibration/response, support, constraint, and component state & Component unavailable or failed; no amplitude-derived role. \\
Source-associated amplitude & Fit-amplitude component plus established association & No source-attributed amplitude; numerical fit component remains visible. \\
Unbiased pointing or correction-use claim & Displacement plus every named-use-required response center, centroid bias, uncertainty, and pointing-support policy & Named-use eligibility is \path{ineligible} or \path{decision_unavailable}; missing bias is not zero. \\
Formal errors & Conforming fit and approved formal-error method & Formal errors unavailable; fitted values may remain. \\
Formal standardization & Exact selected signed fit-amplitude role; approved formal-error method; finite positive formal amplitude error & Independently requested signed diagnostic unavailable. An absolute-magnitude diagnostic is a separate unadmitted identity. \\
Dynamic-range diagnostic & Exact selected signed fit-amplitude role; approved full-map-RMS method; compatible parent/generation; finite positive denominator; claim-appropriate association & Independently requested signed diagnostic unavailable. \\
Photometric transfer & Source-associated amplitude plus CAL/TolProj profile and source/reference authority & Photometric eligibility is \path{ineligible} or \path{decision_unavailable}. \\
Telescope-QC display & Required fit facts plus QC-owner applicability, eligibility, realization, and action & Realization is \path{not_produced}, \path{incomplete}, or \path{failed}; it cannot rescue another use. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\normalsize

Response and covariance availability are evaluated by the applicable row and
named-use policy. Missing response or covariance neither universally erases
all processed-map results nor authorizes response, bias, uncertainty,
correction, calibration, or photometric claims.

\subsection{Uncertainty budget}\label{sec:uncertainty}

Conditional formal fit error, joint parameter covariance, source-reference or
ephemeris uncertainty, WCS/tangent-coordinate uncertainty, parent
response/model-mismatch uncertainty, calibration uncertainty, empirical
pointing repeatability, NOI uncertainty, cross-array dependence, and
pointing-correction uncertainty are separate components with separate owners.
They may be combined only when every variance and cross-covariance needed for
the declared operation is available. Missing covariance is not zero, diagonal
covariance, or independence.

When the fitted-centroid and expected-position covariances are expressed in
one common tangent basis, Equation~\ref{eq:displacement-covariance} governs
their conditional combination. Neither fitted/expected cross-covariance term
may be dropped without independence authority. Coordinate transformations
require their exact Jacobians and complete joint covariance before
transformation. Fit-conditional centroid covariance, source-reference or
ephemeris covariance, AST coordinate uncertainty, parent response/model
mismatch, empirical repeatability, observational centroid bias, cross-array
dependence, and correction uncertainty remain separate.

If fit and published tangent bases differ, exact transformation generally
requires joint centroid covariance. Transforming marginal errors alone through
a non-axis-aligned Jacobian does not produce exact AltAz marginal errors. A
later joint-covariance, astrometric, empirical-repeatability, or NOI companion
is separately versioned and does not rewrite the immutable POINT fit claim.

\subsection{Response and bias separation}\label{sec:response}

POINT can be nonlinear because search, fallback, support, or active constraints
can depend on the data. A fixed-branch response is conditional on one exact
seed/fallback branch, fit support, weight state, and active-constraint set. A
POINT-full-procedure/parent-fixed response reruns every POINT data-dependent
search, fallback, support, constraint, optimization, and association choice
under perturbation while retaining the exact parent product. A whole-chain
full-procedure response additionally reruns the upstream parent producer and
requires separate authority over that complete chain. Observational
centroid bias and pointing accuracy require a separate empirical authority.
Source association is separate from all three. Parent response is input state,
not automatically fitter response; a local Jacobian is not full-procedure
response. A finite-difference full-procedure object is not multiplied as a
Jacobian without an exact composition theorem. Equations~\ref{eq:fixed-response}--\ref{eq:observational-bias}
define the domains and codomains without authorizing a construction. All three
response families and the bias role are presently unavailable under separate
release conditions. Every route still carries its exact parent-response
identity/status, possibly typed unavailable. Numerical response is required
only where the approved fitting method or declared claim depends on it; its
unavailability may coexist with amplitude, centroid, displacement, and other
independent fit roles and blocks only dependent claims. No absent response
implies zero response error or zero centroid bias.

\subsection{Named-use ownership}\label{sec:named-uses}

POINT owns only the per-array fit-completeness policy. The pointing-support
producer owns displacement admission. The named telescope/observing QC process
owns parameter admission and actions. CAL/TolProj owns amplitude admission for
photometric transfer. The same immutable result may pass one use, fail another,
and be shown diagnostically for a third. No state or action propagates across
uses. Failure of one array does not erase siblings; POINT imputes no array and
publishes no observation-wide success. A downstream partial-set aggregate
must record its exact policy and membership.

Only the POINT completeness/publication decision participates in completion
of the base fit atom. Each later named-use decision is an independently
requested child artifact that references the immutable fit, binds its own
profile, source facts, SCI-VAL tuple, lifecycle, cause, and provenance, and
cannot mutate that fit, create a new fit generation, or rescue another use.

\subsection{Claim classes and evidence ceiling}\label{sec:claim-ceiling}

This contract establishes scientific meaning and conditional engineering
conformance requirements. It does not establish representation fidelity,
implementation conformity, numerical production, response or covariance
fidelity, uncertainty coverage, observational validation, pointing accuracy,
performance, readiness, production suitability, production authorization, or
Unity activity.
